clue.text: An honoured team, it's obvious

definitions.note: the definition is a phrase standing for a self-evident statement

parts.note: XI, eleven in Roman numerals, is a cricket or football side
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour, so an honoured person may hold the OM

explanation.surface: A team that has won honours is plainly the best.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces appear in a different order from the clue: A, then XI (the team), then OM (the Order of Merit, a British honour).
explanation.definitionFit: A self-evident truth needing no proof is something plainly obvious.

clue.text: Not so busy types sent in a busy type's. place

indicators.note: in says one word goes inside the letters of the busy type's

parts.note: a busy bee is the stock busy type, so a bee's gives the letters

explanation.surface: Idle workers were sent to stand in for a hard-working one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ... place' reads as a substitution, but 'in' puts SENT inside A BEE'S, after the B.
explanation.definitionFit: People who are away from work are certainly not busy at it.

clue.text: I would have 'a little island, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I would
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Someone claims a small island for themselves, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: IOM is the Isle of Man, an island between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a fixed expression whose meaning is not the sum of its words, a manner of speaking.

clue.text: Corresponding with a crazy French cat in China

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round

parts.note: Ming is a famous dynasty of Chinese porcelain, so china

indicators.note: crazy says the letters of the French cat are scrambled

parts.note: chat is the French word for a cat

explanation.surface: A mad cat from France turns up in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country but is porcelain, named for the dynasty that made it; 'crazy' scrambles the French cat before 'in' houses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are corresponding agree with each other, as a pair of gloves does.

clue.text: Instruments of law men

explanation.surface: A question about the tools that lawyers use.
explanation.walkthrough: In England a Recorder is a part-time judge in the Crown Court.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodwind pipes played in schools are instruments; in England certain part-time judges bear this title, so they are law men.

clue.text: Said to be part of bread

indicators.note: said tells us the word for part is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: a role is an actor's part

explanation.surface: Rumour has it this is a portion of the loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a piece of a loaf; 'part' is an actor's role.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round individual loaf is a type of bread.

clue.text: 'A man down and dejected

parts.note: a chap is a man
fallen means brought down

explanation.surface: A man who is down and out is depressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapfallen describes a jaw dropping in dismay, so it means dispirited.

clue.text: Keep gratitude in check

indicators.note: in says the gratitude sits inside the word for check

parts.note: a rein is a check or restraint
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A warning to keep one's thanks under control.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for 'thank you'.
explanation.definitionFit: To retain something is to hold on to it.

clue.text: Lose claim to become a bullfighter

indicators.note: to become says the letters change into a new word

explanation.surface: Giving up a claim to be a matador.
explanation.walkthrough: Escamillo is the toreador in Bizet's opera Carmen; 'to become' rearranges LOSECLAIM.
explanation.definitionFit: The toreador who wins Carmen in Bizet's opera is a fictional bullfighter.

clue.text: Located or spotted by ear

indicators.note: by ear says the word for spotted is to be heard, not read

parts.note: spotted means seen, sighted

explanation.surface: A place found or noticed by listening.
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed in a particular spot is situated or positioned there.

clue.text: Spark-from a Roman candle ?

explanation.surface: A spark flying from a firework.
explanation.walkthrough: A Roman candle is a firework, but here 'Roman' points to Latin: the English word for a tiny trace is the Latin word for a spark.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny trace or spark is the English sense; the Latin original meant a spark, so it is a spark as a Roman would say it.

clue.text: Tom comes back with it — that's understood

indicators.note: comes back tells us to read the word for Tom from right to left

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: Tom returns with it, and nothing more needs saying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a man's name; it is a tomcat. 'comes back' turns CAT into TAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tacit is implied or understood without being stated aloud in words.

clue.text: Quiet hymns composed for divine girls

indicators.note: composed suggests music written, but here the letters are arranged afresh

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: Soft hymns written for goddesses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' shuffles P (piano, quiet) together with HYMNS; the musical surface hides the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth these were minor female deities of woods and waters, so semi-divine maidens.

clue.text: Stated that a Berber went back to sea

indicators.note: went back says the word for the Berber is read in reverse

parts.note: the Riffs are a Berber people of the Rif mountains in Morocco
MED is short for the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A claim that a North African returned to the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The Riffs are a Berber people of northern Morocco; 'went back' reverses their name, and the sea is the Mediterranean.
explanation.definitionFit: To affirm is to declare or assert, so the past tense means stated.

clue.text: Erectly but without spirit.?:

explanation.surface: Standing up straight but feeling flat.
explanation.walkthrough: To list is to lean, so doing something without a list is doing it upright: the word split as 'list-less-ly' means erectly.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as 'without a lean' it means upright; in its usual sense it means languidly, lacking energy.

clue.text: Heads a German town, tails, oddly enough, gives the main points

indicators.note: heads says the German town goes at the front of the answer

parts.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr, Germany

indicators.note: oddly enough says the letters of the word tails are jumbled

explanation.surface: A coin is tossed in a German town and the result is the crux of the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads' and 'tails' suggest a coin toss; 'Heads' puts ESSEN first and 'oddly enough' rearranges TAILS into TIALS.
explanation.definitionFit: The essentials of a matter are its fundamental, indispensable points.

clue.text: The revolutionary fork-lift.?

parts.note: a long Italian pasta is twirled round a fork before being raised to the mouth

explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' suggests politics, but it is the turning of the fork, and a fork-lift is the food it lifts.
explanation.definitionFit: Long pasta strands are wound by rotating the fork, then lifted.

clue.text: A weary proceeding for Gray's ploughman

definitions.text: A weary proceeding for Gray's ploughman

parts.words: A weary proceeding for Gray's ploughman
parts.note: Thomas Gray's Elegy says the ploughman homeward makes his weary way; the clue asks for the verb in that line

explanation.walkthrough: Gray's 'Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard' has the line 'The ploughman homeward plods his weary way'.
explanation.definitionFit: To trudge slowly and heavily is exactly what the tired ploughman does on his way home.

clue.text: Like a gooseberry Sid turned up and played around

indicators.note: in a down entry turned up means the whole run is read upwards

parts.note: a gooseberry is an unwanted third person, de trop, French for too many
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sid, an unwanted third wheel, arrived and fooled about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses DE TROP and SID together. Playing gooseberry is British for being the unwanted third person with a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: To disport oneself is to frolic, so the past tense means played around.

clue.text: Wenceslas' instruction in the event of a hold-up'?

explanation.surface: What the Christmas carol king would say if his journey were delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: In the carol Good King Wenceslas calls to his page; telling him to halt would be 'Stop, page!'.
explanation.definitionFit: An order to a servant boy to halt is one sense; a stoppage is also a delay or blockage.

clue.text: Royalty has replanned Southend

indicators.note: replanned says the word has is laid out in a new order

parts.note: the end of South is its last letter, H

explanation.surface: Royalty has redesigned the seaside town of Southend.
explanation.walkthrough: Southend is an English seaside town, but here it is read as 'South end', the H. 'replanned' rearranges HAS into SHA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shah was the monarch of Iran, so the title stands for royalty.

clue.text: Paid to 'girl-friends rather than drill-sergeants ?

parts.note: suitors pay courteous notice to sweethearts, while a sergeant on the parade ground shouts the order to stand still

explanation.walkthrough: The plural means a suitor's courtesies, as in paying someone your respects; the singular is what a drill sergeant barks.
explanation.definitionFit: Courtship gestures are things paid to a sweetheart, whereas the singular is the parade-ground command.

clue.text: "There —— Titania some time of the night" (AMND)

definitions.text: "There —— Titania some time of the night" (AMND)

parts.words: "There —— Titania some time of the night" (AMND)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from Oberon's speech in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, asking what Titania does at night

explanation.walkthrough: AMND is A Midsummer Night's Dream; Oberon says 'There sleeps Titania sometime of the night'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oberon's line says the fairy queen slumbers in her bower at some point each night.

clue.text: Hero achieves eminence amongst top men

indicators.note: amongst says the eminence sits among the letters of the top men

parts.note: aces are the best performers in a field
an eminence is a piece of high ground, such as a hill

explanation.surface: A hero rises to fame among the best people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'achieves' is only a link; 'amongst' puts the high ground inside the top men, aces being experts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek warrior of the Trojan War is the great hero of Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: A desire to write a letter

parts.note: an itch is a restless craving

explanation.surface: Someone longs to write to a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to write' suggests correspondence; the letter is the name of H.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the spelt-out name of the eighth letter of the alphabet.

clue.text: Where to, drink between rounds ?

indicators.note: between says the drink sits with a round on each side

parts.note: each round is a circle, the letter O, so two rounds give two Os
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A drinker asks which bar to visit between rounds of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rounds' looks like rounds of drinks; they are two letter Os. Oporto is the Portuguese city from which port wine takes its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The question asks for a place, and the city of Porto in Portugal fits that place.

clue.text: See the magistrate concerning a lady

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Eve is a woman's name, the first lady

explanation.surface: Seeing the judge about a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: A reeve was a medieval English local official or magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: In old England a reeve was a local officer with judicial duties, much like a magistrate.

clue.text: Got a pain, Bill, man ?

definitions.note: the phrase stands for the verb meaning to hurt, the clue using its past form loosely

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: Someone asks if Bill, a man, has a sore spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; it is an account, AC.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache is to suffer a dull continuous hurt.

clue.text: Status symbol gives right of ownership

explanation.surface: A badge of rank brings with it a claim to property.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble rank such as Lord marks social standing, and a legal deed proving ownership of land is the same word.

clue.text: Religious.1 rite puts a thousand in strange trances

indicators.note: puts in says the pieces are placed inside the other letters
puts in says the pieces are placed inside the other letters
strange says the letters of trances are mixed up

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A ceremony puts a large crowd into weird trances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges TRANCES into SACRENT, and A plus M (Roman thousand) go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Baptism and communion are examples of Christian rites, the ceremonies of a church.

clue.text: Coiffure in, the, musical manner

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical
a style is a manner of doing something

explanation.surface: A hairdo done in a theatrical manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hair' is the 1967 rock musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A coiffure is the way someone's hair is cut and arranged.

clue.text: It shows me, finally, to be correct

indicators.note: shows suggests something on display within, so the end word holds the other inside it

parts.note: finally means at the end

explanation.surface: Something proves I was right in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' is a link; 'shows' signals that the word for 'finally' displays 'me' within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend a text by removing its errors is to make it right.
